definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese New Year decoration made of pine branches and bamboo, placed in pairs at the entrance of homes and businesses to welcome the god of the new year.

examples.japanese: ⟦{玄関|げんかん}→玄関：05003_genkan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{門松|かどまつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}った→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧。
examples.english: We put up kadomatsu at the entrance.

examples.japanese: ⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{商店街|しょうてんがい}→商店街：09391_shoutengai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{門松|かどまつ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}ぶ→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧。
examples.english: When New Year's comes, kadomatsu line the shopping streets.

examples.japanese: {門松|かどまつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{松|まつ}の{内|うち}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{過|す}ぎたら→過ぎる：01219_sugiru⟧⟦{片付|かたづ}ける→片付ける：01192_katazukeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{一般的|いっぱんてき}→一般的：04784_ippanteki⟧だ。
examples.english: It is customary to take down the kadomatsu after the pine decoration period ends.

notes:
Compound of {門|かど} (gate/entrance) + ⟦{松|まつ}→松：02256_matsu⟧ (pine). Pine symbolizes longevity and vitality in Japanese culture.

{門松|かどまつ} are set up in pairs at entrances before New Year's Day and removed after {松|まつ}の{内|うち} (the first seven days of the year in most of Japan, or fifteen days in the Kansai region). They serve as a temporary dwelling for {年神|としがみ} (the god of the new year).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {門松|かどまつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}る→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧ (to put up kadomatsu)
- {門松|かどまつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てる→立てる：01196_tateru⟧ (to set up kadomatsu)
- {門松|かどまつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{片付|かたづ}ける→片付ける：01192_katazukeru⟧ (to take down kadomatsu)
